title: Two sum
prompt: Find the indices of two numbers in an array that add up to a target.
explanation: For each number, the partner you need is target - x. Remember every number you've passed in a map of value → index, and check it before storing.
steps: Walk the array once with a map of value → index.
If target - nums[i] is in the map, return both indices.
Otherwise store nums[i] → i and move on.
gotcha: Check before you insert, so a number isn't paired with itself.
hint: For each number you already know exactly which partner you need. How do you look it up instantly?

title: Longest substring without repeating characters
prompt: Given a string, find the length of the longest stretch of characters with no repeats.
explanation: Keep a window with no repeats. Grow it to the right. When the new character is already inside the window, jump the left edge just past its previous position.
steps: Map each character to the last index you saw it.
For each right, if the char's last index ≥ left, set left = lastIndex + 1.
Record the char's index and update best = max(best, right - left + 1).
gotcha: Only ever move left forward. An old index from before the window must not pull it back.
hint: Longest contiguous stretch that obeys a rule? Grow the right edge, and shrink the left when the rule breaks.

title: 3Sum
prompt: Find all unique triplets in an array that add up to zero.
explanation: Sorting turns "find a pair with sum S" into a two-pointer walk, and makes duplicates sit next to each other so they're easy to skip.
steps: Sort the array.
For each i, run two pointers on the rest looking for -nums[i].
Skip equal neighbors for i, left and right to avoid duplicate triplets.
gotcha: Skipping duplicates is where most bugs are. Skip after you record a triplet, not before.
hint: Fix one number. The other two must sum to its negative. In a sorted array, how do you find a pair with a given sum?

title: Container with most water
prompt: Vertical lines of different heights. Pick two that hold the most water between them.
explanation: Start with the widest pair. The shorter line limits the area, so moving the taller one can never help. Always move the shorter side inward.
steps: Put pointers at both ends.
Area = min(h[l], h[r]) × (r - l), and track the max.
Move whichever pointer has the shorter line.
hint: Start as wide as possible. Which side is it pointless to move?

title: Subarray sum equals K
prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum is exactly k. Numbers can be negative.
explanation: A subarray sum is prefix[j] - prefix[i]. While you walk, count how many earlier prefixes equal current - k. A sliding window doesn't work because negatives break the "grow or shrink" logic.
steps: Keep a running sum and a map of prefix sum → count, starting with {0: 1}.
At each element, add count[sum - k] to the answer.
Then increment count[sum].
gotcha: Seed the map with 0 → 1, or you miss subarrays that start at index 0.
hint: The sum of any subarray is the difference between two running totals.

title: Top K frequent elements
prompt: Return the k values that appear most often in an array.
explanation: Count frequencies, then you need the top k counts. Use a size-k min-heap, or bucket sort by frequency for O(n).
steps: Count each value in a map.
Push (count, value) into a min-heap and pop whenever its size passes k.
The heap holds the answer. Alternatively, put values into buckets indexed by count and read from the highest bucket.

complexity.time: O(n log k), or O(n) with buckets

gotcha: JavaScript has no built-in heap. In an interview, say so and use buckets or a sort, then mention the heap.
hint: Two steps: count everything, then keep only the best k.

title: Merge intervals
prompt: Given a list of intervals, merge every pair that overlaps.
explanation: Once intervals are sorted by start, any interval that overlaps the current one comes right after it. One pass is enough.
steps: Sort by start.
If the next start ≤ current end, extend end = max(end, next.end).
Otherwise push the current interval and start a new one.
gotcha: Use max when extending. A short interval can sit entirely inside a long one.
hint: Overlaps are easy to spot when they sit next to each other. What order makes that true?

title: Daily temperatures
prompt: For each day's temperature, how many days until a warmer one?
explanation: Keep the days still waiting for a warmer one on a stack. Their temperatures only decrease from bottom to top. A warmer day resolves everything colder on top.
steps: Walk the days, keeping a stack of indices.
While today is warmer than the top, pop it and record today - popped.
Push today.
gotcha: Store indices, not temperatures. You need the index to compute the gap.
hint: Each day waits for the next warmer one. Keep the unresolved days somewhere you can pop from the top.

title: Search in rotated sorted array
prompt: A sorted array was rotated at an unknown point. Find a target's index in O(log n).
explanation: At any mid, at least one half is properly sorted. Check whether the target is inside that sorted half's range, and discard the other half.
steps: Standard lo <= hi binary search.
If nums[lo] <= nums[mid], the left half is sorted; otherwise the right half is.
If the target is within the sorted half's range, search there. Otherwise search the other half.
gotcha: Use <= in nums[lo] <= nums[mid]. When lo === mid, the left half is one element and counts as sorted.
hint: O(log n) means halving. After splitting at mid, what is always true of one of the halves?
